verdicts.reason: A: the tiny logo floats top-left, off the headline's axis. The subtitle starts at x≈20 while the headline starts at x≈58, so the left edges are ragged. The product is stranded mid-right with dead space around it, and the copy block feels low. B: logo, headline and subtitle share one centered axis, with the product on the left and the CTA on the right, so it reads left to right as a banner should. The product is small and close to the left edge, and the subtitle runs close to the CTA.

A has nearly the same layout as B, but the SOLSTICE wordmark under the sun icon is squashed into an illegible garble, and it sits off-axis to the left of the headline's center. That breaks brand integrity. B keeps the logo crisp and centered above the headline, with a clear product → message → CTA flow. Its only flaws are minor: the product is small and close to the left edge.

A stacks the text on the left, but its left edges don't line up: the CTA starts at x≈22, the subtitle at x≈45, the headline sits centered around x≈230, and the tiny logo at x≈75. The headline and subtitle are jammed together, the CTA sits tight to the bottom, and the product is pushed far right across a large empty gap. B has a balanced three-zone banner on a shared center axis and readable hierarchy, with only minor polish needed on the small product.
